ratingScale.strong: Multiple relevant high-quality studies or syntheses point in the same direction, with plausible mechanisms and limited serious contradiction.
ratingScale.moderate: Relevant evidence supports the mechanism, but important limitations, heterogeneity or transferability issues remain.
ratingScale.developing: Some relevant evidence exists, but direct causal evidence is sparse, mixed or context-specific.
ratingScale.limited: The pathway is mainly theoretical, prospective or weakly evidenced; absence of evidence is not treated as evidence of no effect.

pathways.label: moves decision rights closer to place
pathways.synopsis: There is credible evidence that decentralisation changes decision rights, leadership and local responsiveness. Evidence linking that change to final outcomes is more conditional and depends on institutional design.
pathways.gap: More causal English evidence linking specific devolved powers to decisions, outputs and final outcomes.

pathways.label: enables cross-service coordination
pathways.synopsis: Place-level authority can make coordination easier, but integration requires relationships, aligned incentives, data and capacity. Current English place-based budget pilots are still generating impact evidence.
pathways.gap: Robust comparative evaluation of integrated place budgets and governance models.

pathways.label: creates scope for earlier intervention
pathways.synopsis: The mechanism is plausible and central to current English reforms, but system-level causal evidence that integration shifts resources toward prevention and reduces later costs is still limited.
pathways.gap: Measure whether integration changes the timing of intervention, not only final outcomes; track costs displaced across organisations and time.

pathways.label: may improve outcomes and avoid later costs
pathways.synopsis: Prevention can be effective in specific sectors, but this map does not yet contain a cross-sector REA sufficient to generalise a single effect size across local public services.
pathways.gap: Sector-by-sector evidence synthesis on preventive interventions, costs, time lags and who captures savings.

pathways.label: changes incentives and financing capacity
pathways.synopsis: Greater local revenue autonomy can increase discretion and growth incentives, but volatility, unequal tax bases, administration and equalisation design materially condition what places can invest.
pathways.gap: English causal evidence on whether retained revenues produce additional productive investment rather than substitution or fiscal risk.

pathways.label: may support local economic growth
pathways.synopsis: The direct fiscal-decentralisation-to-growth literature is mixed, with null, negative and context-dependent estimates. It therefore gives limited confidence in any generic growth assumption and points toward testing specific investment channels, local conditions and time horizons during implementation.
pathways.gap: Identify specific investment channels, local conditions and time horizons rather than estimating one average decentralisation effect.

pathways.label: conditions implementation quality
pathways.synopsis: Capacity is consistently identified as an implementation condition: skills, staffing, leadership, systems and fiscal capability affect whether new powers can be used well. Direct causal estimates of the marginal effect of capacity remain scarce.
pathways.gap: Develop validated, decision-useful measures of institutional capacity and test whether they predict implementation and outcomes after devolution.

pathways.label: creates incentives and scrutiny
pathways.synopsis: Accountability is a credible mechanism through which decentralisation can affect responsiveness and performance, but its operation depends on clear responsibilities, capable scrutiny and usable information.
pathways.gap: Test which local accountability mechanisms change behaviour and outcomes in English mayoral systems.

pathways.label: makes performance visible
pathways.synopsis: Timely, comparable and trustworthy data are repeatedly identified as necessary for accountability and learning. More information is not automatically useful if measures are noisy, poorly aligned or create excessive reporting burden.
pathways.gap: Evaluate which indicators support earlier corrective action without producing gaming, excessive reporting burden or misleading league tables.

pathways.label: mitigates unequal local tax bases
pathways.synopsis: Local tax bases differ substantially and fiscal divergence can re-emerge after initial equalisation. This makes equalisation and risk-sharing important implementation variables when local revenue responsibility changes.
pathways.gap: Estimate behavioural responses to alternative equalisation rules under the new English devolution settlement.

pathways.label: sets standards, equalises and learns across places
pathways.synopsis: Public evidence identifies continuing central functions in standards, fiscal rules, equalisation and system learning. The effective boundary between local discretion and national stewardship is context-specific and should be monitored rather than inferred from organisational form alone.
pathways.gap: Compare stewardship models that preserve local discretion while enabling intervention where performance or fiscal sustainability deteriorates.

pathways.label: sectoral place-based contribution
pathways.synopsis: This initial REA does not yet provide enough verified sector-specific evidence to estimate the causal contribution of devolved cultural and sporting investment to wider place outcomes with confidence.
pathways.gap: Run a dedicated sector REA separating participation, wellbeing, local economic, civic and distributional outcomes.
